studies.title: Bring-up: Apertus 1.5 text policy, 70B start-up, multi-set validation
studies.question: Does the NemoRL + NeMo-Gym mcqa stack train Apertus 1.5 (8B and 70B) on Alps?
studies.finding: Yes. The text conversion matches the release (MedQA 59.2 vs 59.8). 70B start-up peaks at ~415-420 GB per node during the HF load, so it host-OOMs with the checkpoint manager on. Async 70B hung when a vLLM engine died during in-flight weight updates, so those are now off. The multi-set validation (MedQA, MedXpertQA, MMLU-Pro health) smoke test passed on 10-07.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5 RL recipe on AlphaMed (256 x 8 per step)
studies.question: Does the Apertus 1.5 recipe (8 rollouts, clip .2/.28, no KL, lr 1e-6) raise MedQA on 8B and 70B?
studies.finding: 70B: MedQA 64.3 → 68.8 at step 40, then a plateau (+4 pt). No weights were saved because checkpointing was off. 8B: dynamic sampling used ~2 batches per step, so the epoch ran out at step 39.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5-8B, AlphaMed-matched (64 x 8, 300 steps): no-think, thinking, pass-rate filtered + KL
studies.question: Does AlphaMed's recipe give Apertus 1.5-8B a real knowledge gain?
studies.finding: No. The +5-6 pt RL-validation gain is the boxed format: ungradeable answers fall from 9.2 % to 0.4 %, while maj@16 stays flat at 64 and medbench is flat. Thinking reaches 64.0 on RL validation (step 250) but medbench is still flat, apart from MMLU-Pro health +4.9 (~3 SE).

studies.title: Llama-3.1-8B control: KL, entropy bonus, dynamic sampling, adaptive entropy
studies.question: Does the pipeline reproduce AlphaMed on its own base model, and what limits the gain?
studies.finding: Control: 60.4 → 71.5 at step 75. Token entropy collapses from 3.6 to 0.33 by step 50, and answer length later collapses too. Dynamic sampling at step 75 is the best trade-off: medbench MedQA 72.3 with IFEval kept. Adaptive entropy (target 0.5) reaches 73.2 at T 0.6, against 75.8 for AlphaMed-8B. A fixed entropy bonus does nothing at 0.001 and diverges at 0.005.

studies.title: 70B thinking + KL (Apertus 1.5) and Llama-3.1-70B
studies.question: Can 70B runs checkpoint on 10 nodes (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2) and does 70B gain more?
studies.finding: Start-up memory tests from 10-06. Results not written up yet.

studies.title: Six recipes on three test sets (Llama-3.1-8B, --val-multi)
studies.question: Is the gap to AlphaMed-8B real on MedXpertQA and MMLU-Pro health, and does its exact recipe close it?
studies.finding: The gap is real: MedQA 70-72.7, MedXpertQA 16-18.9 and health 60-63, against AlphaMed-8B's 75.9 / 25.0 / 66.9 in the same evaluation. The AlphaMed-faithful recipe does not close it, although faithful step 75 has the best medbench MedQA (73.5).

studies.title: CuratedQA data (174k MCQ from meditronfo_gptoss_v1)
studies.question: Does 9x more MCQ data move MedXpertQA where AlphaMed19K does not?
studies.finding: MedQA 73.6 at step 125 is the best of all val-multi runs, but MedXpertQA stays at 17.6, below the AlphaMed-data runs. Continuing to the full first CuratedQA pass (step 485) or switching to AlphaMed after step 300 (3 passes) gains nothing: MedQA drifts to 70-72, MedXpertQA stays 16-19.

studies.title: Reward only when the answer ends at the box (AlphaMed's stated rule)
studies.question: AlphaMed rewards 1 only 'if the model's response ends with a correctly formatted boxed answer'; our grader takes the last \boxed{} with any text after it. Does the end-anchored reward (punctuation still allowed) change the faithful run? Offline: it removes 0-5 pt of reward (base 29.8 -> 27.5, entds s75 71.4 -> 66.6, faithful s300 and AlphaMed-8B unchanged), so expect little.
studies.finding: Done 15 Oct: no effect. llama8b-alphamed-faithful-end 3660603 (300 steps) tracks faithful 3601795/3604613 within noise: best MedQA 72.3 (s125) vs 72.4, MedXpertQA 19.1 (s300) vs 18.9 peak, health ~60 vs ~61; step-1 train reward 0.39 vs 0.45. The end-of-answer reward rule does not explain the AlphaMed gap (MedXpertQA 25.0).

studies.title: How the update is formed: gradient clipping and prompts per step
studies.question: AlphaMed-8B also scores 5 points more on its own training questions (76.6 vs faithful s300 71.3, T=1), with no larger weight change; does unclipping the gradient (every faithful step is clipped at 1, norm 1.2-2.0) or 128 prompts per step (DeepScaleR) lift the training reward past ~0.65 and close the gap? Plus the T=0.6 run judged at T=0.6.
studies.finding: Done 11 Oct. Clipping is not it: clip5 3637148 best 72.3/18.6/61.6, noclip 3637151 71.2/19.1/60.2 (MedQA/MedXpertQA/health) vs faithful 72.4/18.9/62.0; same ~0.65 reward plateau. 128 prompts/step (p128 3637008) best epoch-1 MedQA of the faithful family, 73.9 at step 150, but MedXpertQA 18.9 unchanged; epoch 2 reward 0.73 on seen questions while answers run away (500 to 1,960 tokens) and validation falls. T=0.6 eval 3637010: the T=0.6 run is worse at its own temperature too (step 300 59.6/12.0/47.6, 15 % unboxed). AlphaMed-8B 75.9/25.0/66.9.

studies.title: Reproduce 'Rethinking MCQ for RLVR' (arXiv 2603.12826) best Llama-8B recipe: self-curated distractors (IDC)
studies.question: Does GRPO+RLOO on MedQA-train with distractors curated by Llama-3.1-8B itself (IDC, T=7) reproduce the paper's MedXpertQA 14.3 -> 20.3 (greedy), vs the same recipe on the original options (paper: 16.3)?
studies.finding: Done 13 Oct. Yes: greedy medbench MedXpertQA IDC s316 20.4 (paper 20.3) vs orig 14.4-15.2, best of all our runs (AlphaMed-8B 23.8); MedQA 71.9, IFEval/ARC kept, PubMedQA -4. Caveat: gold is the shortest option 40 % of the time (orig 23 %).

studies.title: DeepScaleR settings AlphaMed-8B was likely trained with (rollout T 0.6, full-vocab entropy, 2 updates)
studies.question: AlphaMed-8B's config names a deepscaler2 workspace; does DeepScaleR's recipe (rollout temperature 0.6, exact entropy bonus 0.001, 2 updates/step) close the MedXpertQA gap?
studies.finding: Done 10-10. No variant closes the MedXpertQA gap: best 18.8 (exact entropy) vs faithful 18.9 and AlphaMed 25.0; full DeepScaleR MedQA 73.3; T=0.6 alone declines. 1-node twins match, ~20% slower, ~40% fewer GPU-h. In axis1_results (11 Oct).

studies.title: Grid over the settings AlphaMed does not report (lr x updates/step x KL)
studies.question: Does a higher learning rate, fewer/more policy updates per step or dropping KL let the faithful recipe reach AlphaMed-8B on MedXpertQA?
studies.finding: Done 10-10. Only lr 1e-6 works; at 3e-6 every run peaks at step 25 then degrades, at 1e-5 all collapse (two stopped early). No setting closes the MedXpertQA gap (best 18.5 vs AlphaMed 25.0). Fig 6 of axis1_results.

studies.title: Rubric design: one HealthBench theme per question vs criteria grouped by aspect
studies.question: Merging the consensus criteria of every theme that applies gives ~13 criteria per question, ~7 of them checking factual accuracy (53% of the reward). Does training on one theme per question (as HealthBench does), or on the same criteria weighted so that each aspect counts once, avoid the short one-template answers of the merged run?
studies.finding: Both collapse to one-line answers like the merged run (Llama, 200 steps, length term kept, ICRC out; 3636913 / 3636914, 10-11). Own validation .24 -> .81 (one theme) and .30 -> .90 (aspects). Checkpoint checks on the same 64 questions, all merged criteria: tokens 648 -> 79 / 79; Gemma-4 .42 -> .51 (one theme, step 50) / .58 (aspects, step 60). Aspects beat one theme on every aspect but asking for context, but answers still contain errors (Jadelle as an IUD, garbled Portuguese). Shared by all three designs: the length bonus and a reference-free judge. Next: aspects without the length term, then question-specific content criteria. 10-14: DR Tulu's evolving rubrics (Gemma-4-31B writes up to 5 items per question from each group's answers, zero-spread items retired) on the merged rubric without length term: llama31-8b-moove-rubric-drtulu, judge 3660795. Done 10-15 (3664722): consensus-rubric val .39 -> .86, but answers dip to ~270 tokens (step 60) then grow to ~1,900 by step 200, as without length term before. Step-200 evals (10-15): HealthBench .380 full / .269 Pro (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct .222 / .202; aspects .273, aspects-nolen .276 full); AutoMOOVE unanimous-576 vs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 484 wins / 51 losses / 41 ties; medbench MedQA 67.2, MedXpertQA 18.0, IFEval 69.9; OR-Bench toxic refusal .73, pokemon-drugs hallucination .89 brand / .88 generic. Best axis-2 Llama so far.

studies.title: MOOVE consensus-criteria rubric RL (Plumb-4B judge)
studies.question: Does a rubric reward built from MOOVE consensus criteria improve answers without reward hacking?
studies.finding: Llama-3.1-8B goes from .35 to .89 on validation, but it collapses onto one paragraph template and gives an unsafe dog-bite answer (don't wash the wound). Apertus 1.5-8B stays flat (.59 → .64) with low entropy (.76 vs Llama 4.07). 40-step tests with lr 5e-6 and with thinking are done. The length term ranks systems by length (ρ .68/.48 vs .93/.98 without it), so dropping it is proposed. 10-14: same run on the ICLR Apertus-8B MeditronFO (SFT) model launched (apertus8b-meditronfo-moove-rubric 3664777): val .41 -> .74 in 200 steps (flat to step 30), answers 1,655 -> ~200 tokens, so it learns where Apertus 1.5 stayed flat, but shrinks like Llama under the length term. Step-200 evals vs its SFT start (10-15): HealthBench .342 vs .421 full, .209 vs .293 Pro (worse); AutoMOOVE unanimous-576 215 wins / 255 losses / 106 ties (worse); medbench slightly up (MedQA 62.9 vs 60.6, MedXpertQA 15.1 vs 13.7, IFEval 54.0 vs 47.0); OR-Bench toxic refusal .94 vs .84; hallucination .94 / .88 vs .97 / .93.
